The other 12 flags are the sanity checker doing its job across two intentional same-day supply changes (eviction fix + Walmart rescue).

items.root_cause: Four distinct mechanisms behind one alert: (1) includes written from one store's naming cannot see a sibling store's word ORDER ('Chicken Breast Chunk' vs 'chunk chicken breast'); (2) a store's mojibake disarms a correct character class - the rule did not change, the world under it did; (3) a brand-scoped exclude from the 07-15 staples batch was silently doing FIRST-MATCH-WINS protection for a LATER commodity, so it cannot be deleted, only narrowed with a lookahead; (4) five rows are things the rules refuse CORRECTLY, and the sweep has no memory of refusals, so they re-page until blocklisted - known-wrong is the designed valve.

surface_fix.what: 4 rule hunks + 9 known-wrong entries; do NOT run apply-coverage-batch.ps1 blind - these hunks ARE the reviewed batch
surface_fix.exact_change: canned-chicken.include += 'chicken\s+breast\s+chunk\b', 'chunk\s+chicken\s+in\s+water'; breakfast-sandwiches.include += 'croissant\s+\d+\s+sandwiches'; pickled-jalapenos.include += 'jalape\S{1,3}o\s+peppers,?\s+pickled'; frozen-vegetables.exclude: REPLACE 'great\s+value\s+mixed\s+vegetables,' WITH 'great\s+value\s+mixed\s+vegetables,(?![^(]*\(frozen\))'; add-known-wrong.ps1 (exact -Store names from stores.json) for: the 73/27 roll vs ground-beef-93-7, Smithfield seasoned vs pork-tenderloin, Fusia Traditional 81 OZ vs soy-sauce, Boulder 40 CT vs quart-storage-bags, Dole Diced Mango vs fruit-cups, and the 3 drumstick names vs chicken-thighs (retire_when ruling-reversed, evidence cites commit 75cf58d7 and the Brad question in this plan)

items.deviation: THREE deviations, all recorded rather than smoothed over. (1) The plan's pickled-jalapenos token 'jalape\S{1,3}o\s+peppers,?\s+pickled' is UNUSABLE as literally written and it crashed test-auditors (exit 1). audit-coverage-gaps.ps1 line 113 loosens every include with a case-INSENSITIVE -replace '\\s' -> '.{0,25}', which rewrites \S as well as \s, producing 'jalape.{0,25}{1,3}o...' - a nested quantifier that throws. Honoured the intent with an equivalent class carrying no \S: jalape[n\u00f1\u00c3\u00b1]{1,2}o\s+peppers,?\s+pickled. It matches the mojibake spelling, the real n-tilde and the plain n, its loosened form parses, and it routes the Clemente row to pickled-jalapenos while San Marcos keeps matching. Written in the \u00XX escape form because guards.ps1 carries a standing check that flags literal mojibake bytes inside matching rules; with the literal bytes that check fired, with the escapes it reads ok and the parsed regex is character-identical. The underlying case-insensitive -replace in audit-coverage-gaps.ps1 is a real latent defect that makes ANY \S, \W, \D or \B in a commodity rule crash that guard; it is NOT fixed here because it is a structural change to a guard's rule library that this plan never measured. Reported for the next review round. (2) The plan asks for 9 known-wrong entries but enumerates only 8 (5 refusals + 3 drumsticks). Reconciled to 9 by including the 14th semantic finding, Walmart '80% Lean / 20% Fat Ground Beef Chuck Patties, 12 Count', which the plan's own do_not_touch rules a correct refusal ('the patties exclude on ground-beef-8020') and which the plan's own root_cause says must be blocklisted or it re-pages forever. (3) Of those 9, only 8 wrote: 'Smithfield Steakhouse Fresh Seasoned Pork Tenderloin' at Walmart was ALREADY blocklisted on 2026-08-02 under key pork-tenderloin|Walmart|smithfield-steakhouse-fresh-seasoned-pork-tender, verdict out-of-scope-variant, not reversed, and covering both name spellings.
